forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Resolution criteria requires (1) a Knesset roll-call vote confirming coalition loss of majority below 61 seats, OR (2) Netanyahu announcing early dissolution AND the election date moving earlier than 2026-10-27. Neither criterion was met: the coalition held 61 seats (one-seat majority) through natural dissolution on July 17, 2026; the election date remained October 27 — not moved earlier. The 'dissolve early' clause in the resolution criteria explicitly requires the election date to shift earlier than Oct 27, which did not occur. The coalition proved more durable than the 0.35 p_prior reflected; F5 tracks the electoral outcome.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

Degel HaTorah files formal dissolution motion in Knesset

forecasts.question: Will Iran publicly commit to resuming mediated ceasefire negotiations (a named Iranian official or MFA announces readiness for talks) before EOD 2026-09-06?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. The September 3-6 window produced the conflict's sharpest bilateral maritime exchange since June: on September 5, US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers in the Strait, permanently disabling two; the IRGC responded with direct missile fire at US warships and issued a statement from IRGC general Rezaei promising more severe attacks. President Pezeshkian's September 1 conditional statement at the SCO summit in Bishkek ('Iran would return to the June MOU if the US carries out its commitments') was not transmitted as an offer of new mediated talks and was followed within hours by mutual exchange of fire. No Iranian MFA official or named senior official issued a formal announcement of readiness for new mediated ceasefire negotiations before September 6. Resolution criteria not met.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-09-06, a named Iranian official (FM Araghchi, Supreme National Security Council, or IRNA/Tasnim/Press TV quoting an official) issues a public statement committing to resuming or entering mediated ceasefire negotiations with the United States. A 'readiness for talks' declaration counts; mere written-message relay does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: One TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera) citing the named Iranian official, OR Iranian state media (IRNA/Tasnim) carrying the official statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Conditional or preconditioned offers ('will talk if US stops strikes') = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless the US publicly accepts the condition; a mediator asserting Iran is 'open' without a named Iranian official statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Araghchi or SNSC public statement committing to talks
Oman or Qatar mediator readout citing named Iranian acceptance

forecasts.question: Will a confirmed Iran-US indirect negotiating session (mediated, senior officials, named principals) occur before EOD 2026-09-17?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. No confirmed Iran-US indirect negotiating session with named senior principals and named mediators took place before September 17. On September 10, Trump stated talks were 'possible within days' — a forward-looking media statement, not a description of an ongoing session. Pakistan and Qatar relayed messages through the period but no bilateral sitting occurred. The ambiguity rule explicitly classifies 'Trump assertions of semi-negotiating without Iranian or mediator confirmation of a held session' as AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. The first qualifying session took place September 23 at UNGA margins in New York — Araghchi and US envoys Witkoff and Kushner in separate rooms with Qatari, Pakistani, and Egyptian mediators shuttling between them — six days after the F3 horizon. Resolution criteria not met.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session (not mere message relay) between named US and Iranian senior officials/envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar/Switzerland), between 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-17.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official mediator readout.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Message relay through intermediaries without a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Trump assertions of 'semi-negotiating' without Iranian or mediator confirmation of a held session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Likud win the most Knesset seats (seat plurality) in the October 27, 2026 Israeli election?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE. Israeli election polls through September 29 show Yashar (Eisenkot), not Likud, holding the single-party lead in four of five surveys. The September 9 i24NEWS poll (Likud 27, Yashar 22) was the sole outlier; the September 23 Channel 13 survey put Yashar at 22 and Likud at 18; the September 29 Kan News poll placed blocs at 52-52 with Yashar at 23 seats and Likud at 21. No formal Likud pre-election alliance with right-bloc partners was announced. The wartime security context did not generate the incumbency boost the 0.42 estimate anticipated; Eisenkot's background as former IDF Chief of Staff has held as a direct counterweight. One Channel 13 survey showed 48% preferring Eisenkot as prime minister vs. 36% for Netanyahu. p lowered from 0.42 to 0.33.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if official Knesset election results published by the Israeli Central Elections Committee show Likud winning more seats than any other single party in the October 27, 2026 election.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Israeli Central Elections Committee official results, carried by Times of Israel/Haaretz/Reuters/AP.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If Likud and one other party tie on seats: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (no plurality). Exit polls alone do not resolve; official preliminary results suffice if published before EOD Oct 27.

indicators.name: Polls showing Likud >=23 seats, ahead of Yashar
Likud bloc forms coalition-eligible alliance pre-election

forecasts.question: Will Iran formally transmit a written response to the US counterproposal (received September 30) through Qatari mediators before EOD 2026-10-04?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Iran received the US counterproposal on September 30 via Qatar; Foreign Minister Araghchi confirmed the content was under review with Tehran leadership (CBS News, September 30). Historical pattern in this conflict: Iran has transmitted written responses to formal proposals within 1-3 days in prior rounds. Araghchi's own prior deadline framework creates a reciprocal expectation. However, the US counterproposal contents were not disclosed and may require Supreme Leader consultation; the IRGC's late-September mine-laying operations and Trump's 'doomsday war' language add friction. Base rate for a written mediator-transmitted response within 72 hours: approximately 55%.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IRNA, Reuters, AP, AFP, or a named Qatari/mediator official confirms Iran transmitted a written response through Qatari mediators before EOD October 4, 2026. NO if October 4 passes with no confirmed transmission reported by named source.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP primary; IRNA or Tasnim accepted as corroborating source when attributed to a named official. Mediator statement from Qatar MFA sufficient.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If Iran makes substantive public statements on its position but no mediator-confirmed written transmission is reported, score AMBIGUOUS.

indicators.name: IRNA or Araghchi public statement confirming response transmitted to Qatar
indicators.expected_effect: Triggers YES resolution if confirmed before EOD Oct 4

The bilateral exchange-of-fire pattern since the June MOU collapse has averaged approximately one publicly acknowledged strike cycle per 7-14 days: CENTCOM struck Iranian oil tankers September 5 (acknowledged); IRGC fired on US warships September 5 (acknowledged); CENTCOM struck Iranian mine-laying assets on a Hormuz island in late September (acknowledged); IRGC launched ballistic missiles and drones at US bases in response (acknowledged). Iran threatened 'more severe attacks' following Trump's September 27 rejection of the road map. The current window — immediately following Iran's receipt of the US counterproposal — is historically a high-tension period before any diplomatic response. Base rate given documented pattern: approximately 60%.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if an official CENTCOM press release, official IRGC statement via IRNA/Tasnim, or Reuters/AP/AFP attributed to a named US or Iranian defense official confirms an offensive strike on the other's military assets before EOD October 8, 2026. NO if October 8 passes with no such acknowledged strike.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: CENTCOM.MIL press releases; IRNA/Tasnim IRGC official statements; Reuters/AP/AFP attributed to named defense officials. Social media claims without official attribution do not qualify.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If strikes occur but neither side officially acknowledges them within the horizon, score AMBIGUOUS.

Trump stated a deal was unlikely before the November 3 US midterm elections, establishing the post-midterm window (November 4-15) as the primary near-term opportunity.
